criteria.blocker: NOT the prerequisite the closure ledger worried about -- a live local database DOES exist, so the ledger's CODE reclassification reasoning is sound. It is open on substance: the legal-hold drill never invokes any production retention or erasure path. It asserts its own hand-written SELECT against a table it just INSERTed into, and its pass/fail predicate is a pure tautology. At head 10 of the 15 cron retention sweeps contain no legal-hold reference at all, so the drill's green cannot mean what the criterion needs it to mean.
criteria.clauses_failing: Run retention/legal-hold drills -- the legal-hold drill is vacuous with respect to production code, and the retention drill recorded in the bundle is a self-declared vacuous pass. The second clause, 'store a redacted, hashed evidence bundle', HOLDS.
criteria.evidence:
PREREQUISITE CHECK FIRST (the thing I was asked to test). A live local Postgres exists and holds real rows: `psql -h localhost -d postgres -c "select datname from pg_database"` lists 124 databases including scratch_head_1010, scratch_cold_1010 and scratch_drill_1010. `check:retention-coverage` ran against one at gate-capture time and measured real data -- /tmp/beg-check_retention-coverage.log reports summary {highGrowthTables: 14, covered: 8, keepForever: 6, uncovered: 0} with kb_article_chunks at 497 MB / 30000 rows and helpdesk_tickets at 220000 rows, exit 0. So the ledger's stated reason for moving PRD-C188 from DEFERRED to CODE ('all of it runs against a local database') is CORRECT and this criterion is not blocked on an absent environment. It fails on its own terms.

FAILING CLAUSE - 'run retention/legal-hold drills'. (a) The legal-hold drill does not exercise production code. /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-backend/src/scripts/drill-legal-hold.mjs is 199 lines. Its verdict function is a tautology: :39-44 `function holdCheck({ hrActive, orgActive }) { return { erasureBlocked: hrActive, retentionBlocked: hrActive, orgPurgeBlocked: orgActive, erasureAllowedAfterRelease: !hrActive && !orgActive }; }` -- 'retention is blocked' is DEFINED as 'an HR hold is active'. The run steps do the same: :136-140 INSERTs into hr_legal_holds, then :142 passes 'Erasure blocked' on nothing more than `activeHrHold(tx, user.id)` (its own SELECT at :87), and :145-151 passes on a second hand-written `SELECT 1 FROM hr_legal_holds` -- the PASS text says so out loud: 'Retention sweep blocked: hold check QUERY returns the active hold'. GdprSubjectErasureService, RetentionService, legal-hold-check.helper.ts and every cron sweep are absent from the script. The stored run confirms this is what was recorded: evidence/42-production-ops/RB-10-privacy-compliance/runs/03-drill-legal-hold.txt, 'PASS 9/9, EXIT_CODE=0', every line an assertion about the drill's own query.

(b) The production sweeps largely do not consult a hold, so the drill's green is false comfort. Measured at head over the 16 retention/purge services in src/modules/cron/, counting `legalHold|legal_hold|hrLegalHolds|organizationLegalHolds`: ZERO in cron-ai-usage-retention, cron-announcements-retention, cron-build-retention, cron-gdpr-export-retention, cron-kb-chunk-retention, cron-mail-retention, cron-notification-outbox-retention, cron-notification-retention, cron-outbox-retention, cron-retention-scheduler and cron-storage-sweep. Only cron-helpdesk-retention (1), cron-hr-retention-documents (2), cron-hr-retention (3), cron-kb-chat-retention (11) and cron-org-purge-worker (7) reference one. The shared helper src/modules/hr/governance/legal-holds/legal-hold-check.helper.ts exports isUnderLegalHold and subjectsUnderLegalHold, and its only production importer is hr/governance/retention/retention.service.ts:18.

(c) The retention half of the drill, as stored, measured nothing. The bundle's own README records run 05 as 'Vacuous pass -- F-3. highGrowthTables: 0; nothing measured' and 05b (--threshold-mb=0.001) as 'Still 0 tables -- proves the integer-division bug'. That bug is still in the code at head: src/scripts/check-retention-coverage.mjs:291 `pg_total_relation_size(c.oid) / 1048576 AS total_mb` is integer division, and there is still no anti-vacuity floor before `process.exit(0)` at :351. It happens not to be vacuous today only because the shared scratch database has grown.

(d) The bundle is not at the release commit. evidence/42-production-ops/RB-10-privacy-compliance/README.md cites backend 45f8a2e99 and frontend 7469d2789. Neither is head. `git diff --stat 45f8a2e99..HEAD` over the gdpr / hr-governance / platform / cron / drill-script paths shows 19 files and +1,231/-179 lines changed since, including gdpr-subject-erasure.service.ts, gdpr-subject-erasure-identity.ts and cron-outbox-retention.service.ts -- the remediation commit's own message names 'gdpr erasure destroyed a multi-org user's GLOBAL identity' as one of the defects it fixed. The stored drill runs therefore describe code that has moved.

CLAUSE HOLDING - 'store a redacted, hashed evidence bundle'. The bundle exists at /Users/tarunchintakunta/Personal/streamline/streamlineos-frontend/architecture-refactor/final-refactor/evidence/42-production-ops/RB-10-privacy-compliance/ with 22 verbatim run files under runs/, a README stating its redaction posture (every subject synthetic on the reserved .invalid TLD, scanned for the scratch password / Neon host / Upstash host / AWS key prefixes before sealing) and per-directory artifact-hashes.json seals. The seal verifies at head: /tmp/beg-check_evidence-seal.log shows '6 seal(s) verified - 73/73 sealed files match - 0 broken / OK -- every evidence seal holds', exit 0.
